 Veterans Day 2026: Here’s what’s open and closed
 By Daniel Miller FOX Local Holidays Published  November 6, 2026 2:15 PM EST Share
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Reddit 
 Published  November 6, 2026 2:15 PM EST article FILE-Members of the U.S. Navy participate in the 106th annual Veterans Day Parade on November 11, 2025, in New York City. (Photo by Spencer Platt/Getty Images) 
 The Brief
 Veterans Day is celebrated on Wednesday, Nov. 11, across the country. 
 Post offices, banks, schools, and federal offices are closed in observance of the federal holiday. 
 Most restaurants and stores are open, but consumers should check the hours of the businesses in their area. 
 The nation will commemorate veterans and active-duty service members on Veterans Day and some businesses and services won’t be available on Wednesday, Nov. 11, in observance of the federal holiday.
 Here is what’s open and what’s closed on Veterans Day.
 Government
 Most federal offices and court buildings have been closed due to the government shutdown, which is now the longest in U.S. history. 
 Post office
 The  U.S. Postal Service (USPS) is closed with no regular mail or package delivery.
 Privately owned delivery services like  UPS and  FedEx , will be open, but consumers should visit their websites to check their hours. 
 RELATED:  VA launches new program to help veterans struggling with home loans 
 Banks and stock market
 U.S. stock markets are open for trading as usual, but the bond market and most banks are closed.
 Retail stores and restaurants
 The vast majority of major retailers — including Walmart, Home Depot and Target — will be open, with many trying to lure customers with promotional sales. Hours may vary by location.
 RELATED: Veterans Day 2026 deals: Where veterans can get free meals and discounts 
 Most restaurants are open on Veterans Day, with some even offering  deals, discounts and freebies.  
 What is Veterans Day?
 The backstory:
 Veterans Day, originally known as Armistice Day, was a holiday first established by President Woodrow Wilson in 1919, marking the one-year anniversary of the end of World War I. The armistice, signed between the Allies and Germany, took effect on the "eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month" in 1918, symbolizing a hopeful end to end the war, according to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs . 
 The Source: Information for this story was provided by the Post Office and U.S. Office of Personnel Management, and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. This story was reported from Washington, D.C.
